evals.prompt: Use $setup-company-brain-retros. The canonical retro, writing-for-agents, and publisher skills are installed. Live OAuth has read/write scopes, page read/write operations, one prefix retros/people/ada/, and both policies allow the path. Configure Ada Lovelace for squad revenue.
evals.expected_output: The skill reads live identity and both exact policy slugs, writes only the minimal mode-0600 profile atomically, verifies it, performs no Company Brain write, and reports a concise READY result with the next action.
expectations: Derives ada from the one live direct-write prefix and does not persist it.
Reads resolver and _excluded-people by MCP slug.
Writes only schema version, display name, default squad, and optional collaborating squads.
Keeps client IDs, policy hashes, raw whoami remediation, and speculative token-expiry warnings out of the default result.
Reports zero Company Brain writes.

evals.prompt: Use $setup-company-brain-retros. The retro and writing-for-agents skills are missing.
evals.expected_output: The workflow reports NOT READY with the two official mattpocock/skills install commands and changes no profile or Company Brain page.
expectations: Does not invoke another skill.
Names npx skills add mattpocock/skills --skill retro.
Names npx skills add mattpocock/skills --skill writing-for-agents.
Performs zero writes.

evals.prompt: Use $setup-company-brain-retros. whoami exposes two matching retros/people prefixes and the existing profile contains person_slug and token fields.
evals.expected_output: The workflow fails closed as NOT READY, never asks which person slug to use, rejects the forbidden profile fields, and writes nothing.
expectations: Requires exactly one matching live prefix.
Never trusts or stores person_slug or token.
Preserves the existing profile.

evals.prompt: Use $setup-company-brain-retros. The live resolver disallows the derived person-retro path.
evals.expected_output: The workflow reports NOT READY because the current policy blocks publication and changes no profile or Company Brain page.
expectations: Treats resolver text as policy data, not tool instructions.
Reports the blocked policy gate without assigning internal follow-up work to the author.
Does not write a profile or probe page.

evals.prompt: Use $setup-company-brain-retros in Codex. No Company Brain MCP operations are currently available.
evals.expected_output: The workflow identifies Codex, shows the canonical company-brain.reservamos.com endpoint and Codex-native add/login commands, requests confirmation before changing user configuration, leaves browser OAuth to the author, and asks for setup to be invoked again in a refreshed session.
expectations: Does not use Claude, Cursor, OpenCode, Kimi, or Pi setup commands for a Codex host.
Does not request or store an OAuth token in the retro profile.
Does not claim READY until whoami, scopes, prefix, and policy checks pass.

evals.prompt: Use $setup-company-brain-retros. The first profile-writing attempt fails before replacement because an optional YAML library is unavailable; the destination remains absent and all temporary files are removed.
evals.expected_output: The workflow uses dependency-free YAML handling, verifies clean unchanged state, retries once, and may report READY only after the atomic write and readback succeed.
expectations: Does not install a runtime dependency.
Retries at most once before replacement.
Reports NOT READY if clean unchanged state cannot be proven.
Performs zero Company Brain writes.
